proof.text: If $X$ is empty, take $T=X$, $g=\mathrm{id}_X$, $d=1$, and the empty family of summands; all fibre and filtration assertions are vacuous. Henceforth assume $X\ne\varnothing$. The affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian by the single affine chart and quasi-compact by the affine quasi-compactness theorem, hence Noetherian. The finite-component theorem gives finitely many irreducible components $Z_1,\ldots,Z_s$.

Partition the finite set of irreducible components by the equivalence relation generated by $Z_i\cap Z_j\ne\varnothing$. For each class take the union of its $Z_i$. Each such union is connected: an irreducible component is connected, and adjoining a component meeting the preceding connected union preserves connectedness (a separation would separate one of these pieces). Each union is closed, and its complement is the finite union of the other classes, hence is closed too. We obtain finitely many nonempty connected open-and-closed subschemes $X_j$. By the clopen-idempotent theorem write $X_j=D(e_j)$ with $e_j^2=e_j$ in $A$. The principal-localization open immersion identifies $X_j$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A_{e_j}$, so it is affine. These are the connected components; no assertion that the irreducible components are disjoint is used.

source.place: Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition); schemes.tex Tag 01I3; elementary finite intersection-graph argument

proof.text: Fix one $X_j$ and a geometric point $\bar x_j$. Apply the finite-coefficient clause of the lisse representation equivalence to $F|_{X_j}$. Its fibre is a finite $\Lambda$-module $M_j$ with a continuous $\Lambda$-linear action $\rho_j$ of $\pi_j=\pi_1(X_j,\bar x_j)$, and $\ell^nM_j=0$. Only clause (1) is used; neither invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$ nor any adic hypothesis is required.

Let $Q_j=\operatorname{im}(\rho_j)\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}_\Lambda(M_j)$. This is finite since $M_j$ is a finite set. The kernel is open: it is the intersection, over the finitely many $m\in M_j$, of the open stabilizers of $m$ supplied by continuity of the action on the discrete module. Thus $\rho_j:\pi_j\twoheadrightarrow Q_j$ is continuous for discrete $Q_j$. Choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $H_j\leq Q_j$ using the prime-index theorem. Put $K_j=\rho_j^{-1}(H_j)$ and $d_j=[Q_j:H_j]$. Then $K_j$ is open and $[\pi_j:K_j]=d_j$, by the bijection $\gamma K_j\mapsto\rho_j(\gamma)H_j$. In particular $d_j\geq1$ and $\ell\nmid d_j$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ0 (lemma-pullback-filtered-modules), finite-monodromy and Sylow part of proof; elementary finite-set continuity and coset calculation

proof.text: By the open-subgroup correspondence choose a connected finite etale cover $v_j:V_j\to X_j$, pointed over $\bar x_j$, for the subgroup $K_j$ (changing the pointing conjugates both subgroup and representation, which does not change the assertion). Its degree is $[\pi_j:K_j]=d_j$. The fundamental Galois equivalence identifies the induced fundamental-group image with this stabilizer and identifies pullback with restriction to it. Apply this to the underlying finite locally constant set sheaf; the natural fibre identification respects addition and each scalar multiplication, so it is also the identification of $\Lambda$-module representations. Consequently $v_j^{-1}F$ has fibre $M_j$ with action factoring through $H_j$. The finite-etale degree theorem makes every geometric fibre have $d_j$ points; since $d_j>0$ this also proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0DV6 (remark-functorial-locally-constant-on-connected); Tag 0GJ0 proof; Section 03SH, finite-etale degree and geometric fibres

proof.text: Apply the primary $\ell$-group filtration theorem to the finite additive group of $M_j$ with its restricted $H_j$-action; $\ell^nM_j=0$ implies that this additive group is $\ell$-primary. It gives a finite increasing chain of $H_j$-stable additive subgroups $0=W_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq W_r=M_j$ with $h w-w\in W_i$ for $w\in W_{i+1}$ and $h\in H_j$. The theorem allows $M_j=0$ and $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GIZ (lemma-action-l-group), finite primary specialization; existing additive filtration node

proof.text: Set $N_i=\Lambda W_i$, the submodule consisting of finite sums $\sum_b\lambda_b w_b$ with $w_b\in W_i$. Then $N_0=0$, $N_r=M_j$, and the $N_i$ form an increasing $H_j$-stable chain. For $z=\sum_b\lambda_b w_b\in N_{i+1}$, $h z-z=\sum_b\lambda_b(h w_b-w_b)\in N_i$ because the action is $\Lambda$-linear. Thus $H_j$ acts trivially on $N_{i+1}/N_i$. This explicitly supplies the required $\Lambda$-submodules, rather than mistaking the additive $W_i$ for $\Lambda$-submodules. Each quotient is finite as a set since $M_j$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0GIZ (lemma-action-l-group): elementary scalar-span upgrade of the existing additive filtration

proof.text: Use the finite-coefficient exact equivalence on the connected scheme $V_j$ to take the invariant submodules $N_i$ to submodule sheaves of $v_j^{-1}F$. Fullness gives their inclusion maps and exactness identifies the sheaf quotients with the objects corresponding to $N_{i+1}/N_i$. A constant finite $\Lambda$-module sheaf with value $B$ has fibre $B$ and trivial monodromy: each element is the value of a global constant section, fixed by every natural automorphism of the fibre functor. Hence the equivalence sends that constant sheaf to the trivial representation $B$; full faithfulness identifies each quotient sheaf with the constant sheaf of $N_{i+1}/N_i$. This gives the finite filtration, allowing repeated terms and zero quotients.

source.place: Tag 0DV5 (3), exact finite-coefficient correspondence; Tag 0GJ0 final filtration paragraph

proof.text: Each $V_j$ is affine because $v_j$ is finite, hence affine, over affine $X_j$. Write $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$; $B_j$ is finite over $A_{e_j}$. Since $e_j$ is invertible and idempotent in $A_{e_j}$, it equals $1$ there; conversely its image in $A/(1-e_j)$ is $1$, so the localization universal property gives $A_{e_j}=A/(1-e_j)$. Thus the same finite generators of $B_j$ generate it over $A$. Set $d=\prod_jd_j$ and $c_j=\prod_{k\ne j}d_k$, so $c_jd_j=d$. Take $c_j$ separate copies of $V_j$, each carrying the filtration just constructed. Their finite coproduct $T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\prod_j B_j^{c_j}$ by the affine coproduct theorem. This product is finite over $A$: take the union of the finite generating sets embedded in the individual coordinates. Put $C=\prod_j B_j^{c_j}$ and choose its finite $A$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_N$. For any affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, its inverse image is $T\times_XW=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A R)$ by the affine fibre-product theorem. This is affine, and $C\otimes_A R$ is generated over $R$ by $b_1\otimes1,\ldots,b_N\otimes1$: expand every tensor using the generators of $C$. Thus $g$ is affine and finite on every affine open, exactly as required by the finite-morphism definition.

source.place: Tag 01S6 (affine definition), finite-morphism affine criterion; elementary finite-product module generators; schemes.tex Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes), 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines)

proof.text: For every summand the map to $X$ is $v_j$ followed by the open immersion $X_j\hookrightarrow X$, so it is etale by open-immersion etaleness and composition. The finite coproduct map $g$ is etale. Each geometric point of $X$ belongs to exactly one $X_j$, and its fibre in $T$ is the union of $c_j$ fibres of size $d_j$, hence has $c_jd_j=d$ points. Since all $d_j$ are positive and prime to $\ell$, so is $d$; these nonempty fibres prove $g$ is surjective. The coproduct inclusions are open and closed and their sources are affine. On each copy, restriction of $g^{-1}F$ is $v_j^{-1}(F|_{X_j})$ by the inverse-image composition identification, so the filtrations from step 8 are exactly the required filtrations on the affine clopen summands $T_a$. For the last identification use the abelian inverse-image composition theorem; its naturality with respect to each scalar endomorphism makes the identification $\Lambda$-linear, and hence an identification of module sheaves.

title: Prime-to-primary finite etale filtration cover for finite local systems
statement: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine with $A$ a Noetherian commutative ring [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], etale locally constant with finite module fibres [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Suppose $\ell$ is prime, $n\geq1$, and $\ell^n F=0$. There is a finite etale surjective morphism $g:T\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and an integer $d\geq1$ prime to $\ell$ such that every geometric fibre of $g$ has $d$ points [def-weil-pbc-geometric-fibre]. Write $g^{-1}F$ for module inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Moreover, $T$ is a finite disjoint union of affine open-and-closed subschemes $T_a$, and for each $a$ the restriction of $g^{-1}F$ to $T_a$ has a finite filtration $0=F_{a,0}\subseteq F_{a,1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_{a,r_a}=g^{-1}F|_{T_a}$ by $\Lambda$-submodule sheaves whose successive quotients $F_{a,i+1}/F_{a,i}$ are constant sheaves of finite $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Empty schemes and zero sheaves are allowed.
